name: Handle a student who misses a quiz without recording a false zero
priorityReason: A quiz average pulled down by a zero the student never earned misrepresents them, and quizzes are frequent.

goal.capability: to mark a student absent from a quiz and decide whether to offer a makeup
goal.outcome: a missed quiz is left out of the average rather than counted as a failure, and I can put it right without a committee

secondaryActors.involvement: Is told their child missed the quiz, and told the result if a makeup is taken.

additional.description: An online quiz window closes with a student who never attempted it, which marks them absent automatically.

preconditions.condition: A quiz exists and is being marked.
An authenticated session exists and the quiz belongs to the acting teacher's subject.
For an online quiz, the attempt window has closed.

postConditions: The student carries Absent for that quiz rather than a score of zero.
The quiz is left out of their quiz average, so an average they never earned a zero on is not pulled down by one.
The teacher decided whether to offer a makeup, without needing coordinator approval or an admin release.
Where a makeup was taken the score replaced the Absent flag and is tagged as a makeup.
Where no makeup was offered the quiz stayed out of the average and the absence stands on the record.
The guardian was told the quiz was missed, and told the result where a makeup was taken.
The Coordinator can see quiz absences across classes, so a pattern is visible even though each quiz is informal.
Nothing about the formal examination flow was involved. A quiz absence needs neither classification nor approval.

businessRules.rule: The teacher may mark a student Absent instead of entering a score. For an online quiz, a student who never attempts it within the window is marked absent automatically.
An absent quiz is left out of the student's quiz average rather than counted as zero. A zero says they attempted it and answered nothing, which is a different and false statement.
Absent is a state on the quiz mark, and the score field is closed for it, exactly as for a formal exam.
The teacher decides whether to offer a makeup. Because a quiz is informal this needs neither coordinator approval nor admin release, and requiring one would mean quizzes are never put right.
Where a makeup is offered the teacher either reopens the online quiz for that student with a new window, or gives them the printed quiz and marks it by hand.
The makeup score replaces the Absent flag and is tagged as a makeup, so a mark earned in a second sitting is distinguishable.
Where no makeup is offered the quiz stays out of the average and the absence stands on the record. Nothing is counted as zero by default.
The Coordinator can see quiz absences across classes. A student missing quizzes repeatedly is a pattern worth seeing even though each quiz is informal.
The guardian is told the quiz was missed, and told the result where a makeup is taken.
A student absent from the makeup too is recorded absent again, and the quiz stays out of the average.
None of this touches the formal examination flow. A quiz absence needs no classification, no approval and no release.

outOfScope.item: A missed formal examination, which needs classification and approval

handledBy.name: Recording a student absent from an exam
Makeup exam for an absent student

departures.requirement: There is no route by which a missed quiz becomes a zero. It is either left out of the average or replaced by a makeup score.
A teacher can mark an absence and offer a makeup without any approval step, because a quiz needing a committee is a quiz nobody puts right.
The quiz average recalculates the moment an absence or a makeup score is recorded.
Quiz marks and absences are retained for the academic session and its reporting.

openQuestions.question: How many quizzes may a student miss before it is escalated beyond the teacher?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The Coordinator can see the pattern but nothing acts on it.

openQuestions.question: Is there a limit on how long after a quiz a makeup may be offered?
Should a makeup quiz score be capped, as a makeup exam might be?
openQuestions.assumption: Not capped as modelled, since a quiz is informal.

openQuestions.question: Does a student who misses every quiz in a term have a quiz average at all?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and an average over nothing is not a figure.

openQuestions.question: Should the guardian be told about every missed quiz, or only a pattern of them?
openQuestions.assumption: Every one as modelled. That may be too many messages.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
